reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown read the terse Kings notice as the same public sacrifice Chronicles narrates fully, with Solomon's nobility assumed present though unnamed.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells sets the bare Kings notice, which names no crowd, directly against Chronicles' report that all the congregation went up with Solomon.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there; for that was the great high place: a thousand burnt offerings did Solomon offer on that altar.
sides.verseText: The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there; for that was the great high place: a thousand burnt offerings did Solomon offer on that altar.

sides.snippet: So Solomon, and all the assembly with him, went to the high place that was at Gibeon; for there was the tent of meeting of God, which Moses the servant of Yahweh had made in the wilderness.
sides.verseText: So Solomon, and all the assembly with him, went to the high place that was at Gibeon; for there was the tent of meeting of God, which Moses the servant of Yahweh had made in the wilderness.
